capability.summary: List named Python blocks and their cyclomatic complexity
capability.description: Reads one source file as text, runs Radon's cc_visit, and returns each discovered block's name and numeric cyclomatic complexity only.
capability.problem_space: Minimal cyclomatic-complexity inspection of functions, methods, and classes in one Python source file.

constraint.io_signature: Input: one Python source file path; output: JSON blocks array whose entries contain only name and complexity.
accepted_inputs: a readable Python source file parseable by Radon's complexity visitor
constraint.output_shape: Success is an object with status="success", tool="lib.radon_complexity", and blocks as an array whose entries each contain name as a string and complexity as Radon's integer cyclomatic-complexity value. A caught file-read, decoding, Python-parse, or complexity-analysis exception produces an object with status="error", tool="lib.radon_complexity", and message as the exception string, then exits with code 1.
limitations: computes cyclomatic complexity only and does not calculate maintainability index despite the original label
returns no block type, rank, line number, column, closure context, or filename
duplicate block names can be ambiguous because only name and complexity are retained
reads exactly one file using Python's default text encoding and does not recurse through directories
file access, decoding, and Python syntax failures use the wrapper's error envelope

output_contract.description: Array of Radon-discovered Python block names with cyclomatic complexity values.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: measure cyclomatic complexity in one Python file
list Python block names and complexity values
negative_intents: calculate maintainability index or Halstead metrics
return complexity ranks locations or full block metadata
